title: Electromagnetics
tagline: Electrostatics, magnetostatics, Maxwell’s equations, plane waves and transmission lines
summary: Circuit theory is an approximation to electromagnetism. This course develops static electric and magnetic fields, capacitance and inductance, Faraday’s law and Maxwell’s equations, and the propagation, reflection and guiding of electromagnetic waves, ending with transmission lines.

chapters.title: Vector analysis for fields
chapters.summary: Coordinate systems, line, surface and volume integrals, gradient, divergence and curl, and the theorems of Gauss and Stokes.

chapters.title: Electrostatic fields
chapters.summary: Coulomb’s law, electric field and flux density, Gauss’s law, and the electric potential.

chapters.title: Conductors, dielectrics and capacitance
chapters.summary: Current and conductors, polarisation and permittivity, boundary conditions, capacitance and electrostatic energy.

chapters.title: Poisson’s and Laplace’s equations
chapters.summary: Boundary-value problems in electrostatics, uniqueness, the method of images and numerical field solutions.

chapters.title: Magnetostatic fields
chapters.summary: The Biot–Savart law, Ampère’s law, magnetic flux density, vector potential and magnetic materials.

chapters.title: Electromagnetic induction
chapters.summary: Faraday’s law, motional and transformer emf, self- and mutual inductance, magnetic energy and forces.

chapters.title: Maxwell’s equations
chapters.summary: Displacement current, Maxwell’s equations in integral and differential form, boundary conditions and time-harmonic fields.

chapters.title: Uniform plane waves
chapters.summary: The wave equation, plane waves in lossless and lossy media, skin depth, polarisation and the Poynting vector.

chapters.title: Reflection and transmission of waves
chapters.summary: Normal and oblique incidence on planar boundaries, standing waves, total internal reflection and the Brewster angle.

chapters.title: Transmission lines
chapters.summary: Distributed circuit models, the telegrapher’s equations, characteristic impedance, reflections, standing waves and transients on lines.
